- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 75–80+ price peaks), then corrects downward — model fails to fully adjust downward after peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high relative to recent 10-day average, especially in the middle of forecast.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to recent price drops; underestimates downward momentum.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts show persistent overestimation in the first 10 days, then underestimation in the last 10–20 days — model “over-anticipates” early moves and “under-reacts” to late corrections.
- Avoid extrapolating recent volatility; model tends to amplify recent trends (especially upward) without sufficient smoothing.
